Key: From Bob’s “give 5 sweets” condition, sums equal ⇒ (A+a)−(B+b)=10 and from Alice’s double‑sum ⇒ A+a=2(B+b). Hence B+b=10, A+a=20. So B+b=10, A=20−a, b=10−B.  

Equations:  
1) (20−a)·a = 4·B·(10−B) (product‑quadruple)  
2) (20−a)(a−5) = B·(15−B) (post‑transfer product equal)  

Search a∈[5,19], B∈[1,10] → unique solution (A,B,a,b) = (10,5,10,5).  

Product of ages = 10·5 = **50**.

Key: Let S_A=A+a, S_B=B+b. From “double” and “give‑5” get S_A=2S_B and S_A=S_B+10 → S_B=10, S_A=20. So a=20−A, b=10−B.  
Equations: A(20−A)=4B(10−B) and A(15−A)=B(15−B).  
Search A≤15, B≤10 → only (A,B)=(10,5). Product = 10·5=50.
